title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: A sorted list of distinct integers was rotated at some unknown pivot (for example [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] became [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]). Return the index of the target, or -1 if it is absent, in O(log n).
brute_force_solution:
def search(nums, target):
    return nums.index(target) if target in nums else -1

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    a = list(range(200000))
    k = 77777
    return [a[k:] + a[:k], 12345]

hints.1_question: After rotation the array is no longer sorted, but what is always true about at least one half when you split at mid?
hints.2_nudge: At each step one half [lo..mid] or [mid..hi] is properly sorted. Check whether the target lies inside the sorted half; if so go there, otherwise go to the other half.
hints.3_big_hint: If nums[lo] <= nums[mid] the left half is sorted: if nums[lo] <= target < nums[mid] hi = mid-1 else lo = mid+1. Otherwise the right half is sorted: if nums[mid] < target <= nums[hi] lo = mid+1 else hi = mid-1.

known_bugs.name: ignores the rotation (plain binary search)
known_bugs.followup: In [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], if nums[mid] = 7 and the target is 0, is the target to the left or right of mid?

known_bugs.name: uses < instead of <= when detecting the sorted half
known_bugs.followup: When lo == mid (two elements left), is the 'left half' sorted? What does your comparison say?

known_bugs.name: checks only one bound of the sorted half
known_bugs.followup: Being smaller than nums[mid] only means 'left of mid' in a sorted half if the target is also at least nums[lo]. Where do you check that?
